still_broken.description: Whenever the user scrolls WITHIN the open detail view to a position different from where it was entered, then exits via the back control (pointer), Escape (keyboard), or a genuine browser/hardware back, a single-frame hard snap to scrollY 0 occurs at roughly t+50ms after the action - well before HEIGHT_HOLD_EXIT_MS (460ms) and before holdDocHeight() has even run (captured: the scroll-to-0 and the resulting 'scroll' event fire BEFORE the 'popstate' event that runs exitDetail; body min-height is still '' at the moment scrollY hits 0, only becoming pinned one frame later). This is not the same mechanism as before (which restored to the entry-time scrollY) - it is a harder, unconditional reset to exactly 0, and nothing in exitDetail() re-asserts the pre-exit scrollY, so it is never corrected. releaseDocHeight's own correction (window.scrollTo to maxScroll) only fires when scrollY > maxScroll, which is never true once scrollY has already been zeroed, so the page never reaches the claimed settle target (573 at 360x780, 547 at 390x844) - it silently stays at 0.

still_broken.note_on_event_order: The scroll event (and the underlying scrollY change to 0) fires BEFORE popstate, i.e. before any of exitDetail's JS runs at all. No scrollTo/scrollIntoView/focus call from the page's own JS was logged before this happens (instrumented via wrapping window.scrollTo, Element.prototype.scrollIntoView and HTMLElement.prototype.focus) - it is the browser's own back-navigation handling, not app code, and it happens regardless of history.scrollRestoration='manual'.

suggested_fix: history.scrollRestoration='manual' stops the browser from restoring a PREVIOUSLY-recorded offset, but does not stop Chromium's own scroll-to-0 step that happens as part of processing a same-document back navigation before popstate fires. The standard remedy for 'manual' mode is for the app to explicitly reassert the scroll position itself in the popstate handler. Concretely: capture window.scrollY into a stashed variable in closeDetail() (js/main.js ~line 1653), alongside the existing pendingExitViaKeyboard stash that already survives the history.back() -> popstate hop, then as the very first line of exitDetail() (before holdDocHeight() and before any DOM mutation), call window.scrollTo(0, stashedScrollY) to put the browser's already-zeroed scrollY back to where the user actually was, before proceeding with the existing height-hold / settle / focus logic.
